Like the AI agents. They broke Git in Anthropic

The video shows how the volume of code generated by AI agents overloaded the traditional version control. It tells how Anthropic created Scion, a system of its own, and how Cloudflare responded with Artifacts. Ends with the next bottleneck, review and approval of the code.

Published in 19 October 2026 · 7 min 7 s

  • Agentic engineering
  • Specification and development

The human age

The version control the industry has used for decades is not supporting the weight of automation 00:00. AI agents are forcing a redesign of these tools. 00:22.

The video quotes Brian Berliner in a 1990 CVS article: the problem was how to deal with multiple developers changing the same file at the same time 00:43. CVS and then Git were born to solve this collaboration on a human scale. 01:05. But this architecture depended on an invisible limit: human rhythm. People stop, sleep and type slowly 01:05.

Agents break the system.

Anthropic felt it in her own numbers. 01:26. In May 2026, the company integrated about 2,500 changes a day. Four months later, in September, they were over 30,000 a day, driven by AI agents 01:48. The result was an overload in the traditional Git and a continuous integration transformed into bottleneck 01:48.

Agents don't stop at the weekend, attack various problems at the same time and produce a volume that crushes flows made for people 02:08. The main problem is not the size of the repository, but the rate of changes 02:08.

The video cites a community observation: the code review worked because there was one person to defend and explain the decisions 02:28. The agent breaks that premise, because it often delivers only the result. Without provenance, the story of why, the review is almost impossible 02:49.

Anthropic and Scion

To solve the crisis, Anthropic built its own system, Scion 03:12. Instead of the client commit, Scion uses changessets and commits and merges it to the server 03:12. The architecture is distributed, and no server saves a full copy of the repository 03:12. The solution was not a better AI tool, but a new way to store the code 03:33.

According to the video, the Scion infrastructure consumes about 200 times less memory and CPU than the previous 03:33. This earned an estimated gain of 25% CPU capacity and took from minutes to seconds the time of continuous integration 03:54.

Cloudflare and Artifacts

Cloudflare faced the same crisis and responded with Artifacts 04:16. It is a distributed file system, with history and state, which speaks the Git protocol natively 04:16. It uses Durable Objects to keep thousands of instances isolated, with a Git engine compiled in WebAssembly 04:16. Thus, it creates repositories on time for agents, without people changing tools 04:37.

For heavy repositories, ArtifactFS avoids waiting for the full clone 04:37:

1. It starts with a clone without blobs, just the file tree 04:58. 2. Lower real content in background 04:58. 3. Gives priority to code manifests before images and binaries 04:58.

With that, the agent starts reading and writing on time 05:19.

The next neck

Generating fast code does not guarantee delivering the fastest product 05:19. With agents, writing the code hardly takes time, but the bottleneck only changed place: the review and approval queues begin to lock the team 05:39.

The new pressure points are 05:59:

  • the capacity of continuous integration 05:59;
  • the speed of tests 05:59;
  • merge conflicts, when many agents move in the same repository 05:59;
  • security, because a failure in access controls grows at the speed of code entering 06:20.

The final question: if agents start generating 30,000 changes a day, who or what system will review, validate and safely approve this code 06:40?

Frequently Asked Questions

Why do AI agents overload Git?

By pace: Agents generate non-stop changes at the same time, and the problem is the rate of changes, not the size of the repository 02:08.

What does Scion change about Git?

Commit and merge on the server, with changesets, and no server saves a full copy of the repository 03:12.

What's the next bottleneck?

Review and approval of the code, which need to monitor the volume that agents generate 05:39.

About the video

Software agentic development is redefining the limits of engineering infrastructure. When autonomous AI agents began to create and modify code uninterruptedly in Anthropic, the tools designed for the human scale reached an inflection point.

In this video, we analyzed in detail how the rate of integrated changes (*merges*) in the company's monorepo jumped from **2,500 to more than 30,000 per day** in just four months, making the use of traditional Git unfeasible. Understand the architecture of **Scion**, a centralized and service-oriented version control system built in just 5 months by a team of 7 engineers with the massive help of Claude himself.

---

**What you will learn in this video:**

• **The Git Physical Limit:** Why assumptions like *offline* support and complete copies of the repository become bottlenecks in environments with agents always *online*.
• **Scion architectural changes:** The replacement of traditional *commits* with *changesets* in Write-Ahead Log (WAL) in Cloud Spanner and the end of package maintenance (*packfiles*).
• ** Client-Server Asymmetry:** How to download derived data (*blame*, history) to the server enabled virtual *checkouts* and high speed sparses.
• ** Verifiable Performance Metrics:** Reduction of **200 times** in infrastructure footprint (CPU/memory), *cache score rate > 99% and *checkout speed* falling from minutes to seconds.
• ** Government with Antique:** The transition to *intent-based revision*, the application of semantic restrictions and the indispensable role of human engineers as *guardrails*.
• * Has Git become Obsolete? * A critical analysis of why Scion is not a universal substitute for Git** and what architectural criteria evaluate corporate adoption.

---
